interaction.prompt: You have the puck in the strong-side corner. X1 has stepped up to cover the slot. Drag your LW to the highest-value position.

read.cue: X1 has stepped up to contest the slot — the net-front directly behind X1 is now unguarded.

feedback.right: X1 stepped up to cover the slot, which opened the net-front behind them. Crashing there gives you a tip or rebound chance and forces the goalie to see through traffic.
feedback.wrong: Staying in the slot looks natural, but X1 has already stepped up and owns that spot. The space X1 vacated — right in front of the net — is where the scoring chance lives.

tip: When a defender steps up to the slot, check for the hole they left behind at the net-front — a defender can't be in both places.
why: X1 stepping up creates an inverse opening: the slot is now covered but the net-front is free. Reading that swap and filling the net-front is the core U11 positioning skill in a cycle.
